Act as a senior professional game developer, gameplay programmer, 3D game engineer, UI/UX designer, animation engineer, and mobile game optimization specialist.

Your task is to BUILD, IMPLEMENT, AND TEST a complete, professional-quality, fully functional endless runner action game titled:

ANIME RUSH: MULTIVERSE ESCAPE

This must be a genuine playable game, not a static visual prototype, landing page, animated background, or collection of decorative UI elements.

The game should combine the addictive three-lane endless runner mechanics of Subway Surfers with original anime-inspired environments, characters, combat abilities, boss encounters, and progression systems.

The game must be designed primarily for Android mobile phones, while also supporting desktop browsers.

CRITICAL DEVELOPMENT INSTRUCTION

Do not merely generate a visually attractive interface or claim that features have been implemented.

Actually implement the underlying functionality.

Every button must perform its intended action. Every character must be playable. Every obstacle must interact with the player. Every animation must work. Every gameplay system must be connected to the main game loop.

Do not replace functional gameplay with static images or decorative animations.

---

Genre:

- Endless Runner
- Anime Action
- Survival
- Combat
- Boss Battles

Game Mode: Single Player.

Platform Priority:

1. Android smartphones
2. Mobile browsers
3. Desktop browsers

The player selects an anime character and enters that character's universe.

A powerful enemy from the selected universe continuously chases the player.

- Run automatically.
- Avoid obstacles.
- Change lanes.
- Jump and slide.
- Collect coins and energy shards.
- Activate special abilities.
- Escape the chasing enemy.
- Defeat bosses at specific milestones.
- Unlock characters, abilities, skins, and universes.

There must be NO trains, railway tracks, subway stations, or conventional Subway Surfers environments.

The game must have its own identity, visual language, mechanics, and progression system.

- A distinct visual appearance.
- An individual character preview.
- An animated idle pose where assets permit.
- Character name and anime universe.
- Character-specific statistics.
- Unique abilities.
- Unlock status.
- Selection indicator.

The selected character must actually appear in gameplay.

Do not use the same generic character model for every selection.

Use properly licensed assets, original assets, or permitted character-inspired artwork. Do not rely on missing external image URLs.

If an animated 3D model is unavailable, use a properly implemented 2D skeletal or sprite animation system with multiple animation frames. Never substitute a single static portrait for the actual player character.

---

4. UNIVERSE SELECTION AND ENVIRONMENT SYSTEM

Create a separate universe selection interface.

Every universe must have a visually distinct environment, lighting, architecture, obstacles, enemies, atmosphere, and soundtrack.

A. NARUTO UNIVERSE

Environments:

- Hidden Leaf Village
- Shinobi War Battlefield
- Forest of Death
- Destroyed Ninja Village

Enemies:

- Rogue Ninjas
- Akatsuki-inspired enemies
- Tailed Beasts
- Powerful Shinobi Bosses

Abilities:

- Rasengan Dash
- Sha

## Objective
- Complete **ANIME RUSH: MULTIVERSE ESCAPE** as a playable mobile-first endless runner with desktop browser support.
- Finish gameplay and progression, connect the selection flow, and validate the game visually and functionally.

## Requirements
- Three-lane running with lane changes, jumping, sliding, collectibles, abilities, chase/boss encounters, and progression.
- Include all 13 characters and show the selected character in gameplay.
- Distinct selectable universes and environments; no trains, railway tracks, or conventional Subway Surfers settings.
- Functional buttons and gameplay; original or permitted artwork without missing external image assets.
- Save small JPEG screenshots (viewport ≤1280px) for checks and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use standalone HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with canvas-rendered character/environment art and no external art assets.
- Use localStorage for currency and personal-best persistence; use procedural audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built home, character and world selection, guide, pause/result screens, HUD, responsive styling, and touch controls.
- Added all 13 character definitions, four worlds, selection rendering, navigation, input handlers, and persistence.
- Added canvas rendering for the environment, runner, obstacles, collectibles, boss, and HUD.
- Added “CHOOSE THIS RUNNER” to proceed from character selection to world selection.
- Implemented gameplay loop, spawning, pickups, collisions, health, energy abilities, boss encounters, scoring, results, and retry flow.
- Fixed pause/resume so the game HUD returns when resuming.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Started a local HTTP server on port `3002`.

### Active
- Validate selection and gameplay end-to-end in a browser, including responsive layout and console errors.
- Fix issues found in testing and capture and inspect the latest JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Open the game at `http://localhost:3002` and test character/world selection, controls, pause/resume, collisions, boss encounters, and retry.
2. Check browser console errors and mobile layout; fix any issues.
3. Save and inspect a JPEG screenshot at a viewport no wider than 1280px.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Screens, selection flow, HUD, and controls.
- `game.js`: Character/world data, rendering, input, and gameplay systems.
- `style.css`: Responsive interface and game HUD styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Browser verification and screenshot capture have not yet been run.
